A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Hoi! dataset and contain complete, readable main text and supplementary material. All 18 pages were compared; the supplementary pages are identical in text and rendering.

before.justification: V1 reports original trajectory-validation, articulation-estimation, and force-prediction results in Tables 3–6, plus supplementary tactile-force and hand-pose evaluations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical evaluations and their reported results, including Supplementary Tables 7–8.

M1.justification: The Hoi! gripper, data-capture pipeline, sensor alignment, calibration, and force-processing procedures are unchanged, including their supplementary descriptions.

E1.justification: Both versions retain 3,048 sequences across 381 objects and 38 environments, the same embodiments, and the same articulation, tactile-force, visual-force, and supplementary hand-pose evaluations. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding evaluations retain the same methods: GPT-5, ArtGS and ArtiPoint for articulation; Sparsh with DINO and DINOv2 for tactile forces; ForceSight for visual forces; and the Hamer hand-pose baseline in Supplementary Table 8.

E3.justification: Evaluation settings remain identical, including depth scaling, tactile-force clipping, zero-shot ForceSight evaluation, raw versus projected force measurements, and the six-environment supplementary evaluations.

E4.justification: Both retain the raw-versus-projected force comparison, gravity-compensation example in Supplementary Figure 9, tactile underprediction example in Supplementary Figure 13, and exploratory hand-pose analysis in Appendix D.4.

E5.justification: The confidence intervals in Table 5 and Supplementary Table 7 are unchanged, as is the temporal-alignment uncertainty analysis in Appendix B.1. No run-count, seed, or statistical-reporting changes appear.

E6.justification: Tables 3–6 and Supplementary Tables 7–8 retain identical result entries and values. For example, ForceSight's overall projected/raw RMSE remains 2.23/2.57 N, and overall hand-pose PCK remains 0.699. The qualitative findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The supplementary calibration, gravity-compensation, temporal-uncertainty, spatial-alignment, and force-decomposition equations and assumptions are identical. No mathematical definitions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions concerning the multimodal dataset, custom gripper, cross-view observations, and interaction benchmarks. The added website sentence makes no new scientific claim.

C2.justification: Interpretations of depth sensitivity, tactile distribution shift, and force-prediction errors are retained. Section 5 preserves the same embodiment, mechanism-coverage, and policy-learning limitations; Appendix D.4 retains its exploratory-evaluation qualification.

D1.justification: V2 adds a clickable project-website pointer at the end of the abstract, absent from v1. Technical and implementation details remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish that code or data became newly available.

R1.justification: The same 55 cited works and research positioning are retained. Four bibliography page backlinks change because their citations move from page 1 to page 2; these are presentation changes.

P1.justification: V2 adds the abstract sentence 'Further information can be found on the Website' and updates the version/date stamp. The substantive prose, terminology, and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added abstract sentence causes small text-flow and layout shifts, including the vertical placement of Table 6. Figures, table structures, captions, and supplementary layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The direct project-website link modestly improves resource discoverability from the abstract. This is a small usability improvement: scientific content, empirical support, limitations, and appendices are unchanged, and the PDFs alone do not demonstrate a new code or data release.
